raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Part 2 of splitting #25528 (as discussed there with the maintainers; part 1 is #27381). Enables full LoRA support for LFM2 (dense) and LFM2-MoE: attention, MLP, MoE experts (per-expert), MoE router (`gate`), and ShortConv (`in_proj`/`out_proj`). All LFM2-specific logic lives in the two model files.

## Modifications

**Model files (LFM2-specific):**
- **`models/lfm2.py`** — the dense MLP used module names `w1/w3/w2`, but adapter normalization renames those weights to `gate_proj/up_proj/down_proj` and stacks them into `gate_up_proj`, so dense MLP LoRA landed in buffers no module consumes and was silently never applied. Aligned the MLP with `lfm2_moe.py`'s fused naming (`MergedColumnParallelLinear gate_up_proj` + `down_proj`, `SiluAndMul`). Added `get_hidden_dim` (LoRA buffers must use LFM2's *actual* FF dim — `block_auto_adjust_ff_dim` means e.g. `intermediate_size=12288` in config but 8192 in the modules) and `get_stacked_multiply` (ShortConv `in_proj` packs 3 partitions: B/C/x).
- **`models/lfm2_moe.py`** — `get_hidden_dim` (incl. router `gate`: hidden → num_experts; `in_proj`: hidden → 3·hidden) and `get_stacked_multiply`. The router is a `ReplicatedLinear`, handled by the existing `ReplicatedLinearWithLoRA`.

**Core files (generic/additive):**
- **`lora/lora.py`** — generic normalizer: tile a single-rank `lora_A` for adapters trained against a merged multi-partition `in_proj` as one Linear (partition count from the model's `get_stacked_multiply`; weights already stacked by the Mamba/GDN normalizers are shape-guarded out). Same pattern as the existing `in_proj_qkvz` handling.
- **`lora/utils.py`** — `gate` added to known modules; `w1/w3/w2` entries in target-name normalization, mirroring the existing `_rename_expert_w_to_proj` weight rename.
- **`utils/common.py`** — `out_proj`, `in_proj`, `gate` added to the CLI whitelist.
- **`lora/mem_pool.py`** — `has_shared_experts` extended for `num_dense_layers > 0` so hybrid MoEs with leading dense MLP layers (LFM2-MoE: layers 0–1) get their non-MoE 3D buffers alongside the 4D `*_moe` ones. (DeepSeek hybrids already work because they set `n_shared_experts > 0`.)

## Accuracy Tests

Teacher-forced top-k logprob comparison vs HF+PEFT running the same adapters (greedy, bf16):

| Run | ROUGE-L | Prefill mean/max Δlogprob | Decode mean/max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dense base vs base (noise floor) | — | 0.12 / 0.49 | 0.09 / 0.25 |
| **Dense + LoRA** | **1.00 (token-identical)** | 0.14 / 0.44 | 0.17 / 0.43 |
| MoE base vs base (noise floor) | — | 0.37 / 1.50 | 0.40 / 1.75 |
| **MoE + LoRA** | **1.00 (token-identical)** | 0.22 / 0.77 | 0.28 / 0.87 |

With LoRA applied, divergence from HF is at or below each model's no-LoRA kernel-noise floor, and 32-token greedy generations are byte-identical.

**Reproducing — dense (LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct), adapter [`LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-smoltalk-LoRA`](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-smoltalk-LoRA):**

```bash
sglang serve \
    --model-path LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct \
    --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 8 \
    --lora-paths "smoltalk=LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-smoltalk-LoRA" \
    --lora-target-modules q_proj k_proj v_proj out_proj gate_proj up_proj down_proj in_proj \
    --lora-strict-loading
```

**Reproducing — MoE (LFM2-8B-A1B), adapter [`LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B-smoltalk-LoRA`](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B-smoltalk-LoRA):**

```bash
sglang serve \
    --model-path LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B \
    --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 8 \
    --lora-paths "smoltalk=LiquidAI/LFM2-8B-A1B-smoltalk-LoRA" \
    --lora-target-modules q_proj k_proj v_proj out_proj gate_proj up_proj down_proj in_proj gate \
    --lora-strict-loading
```

Generate (same for both):

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:30000/generate \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"text":"Write a short story set in an unusual location.","sampling_params":{"temperature":0.0,"max_new_tokens":80},"lora_path":"smoltalk"}'
```

nodes.body:
> [!WARNING]
> You have reached your daily quota limit. Please wait up to 24 hours and I will start processing your requests again!

Thanks for the thorough review - all blocking issues fixed, details on each thread. Branch is rebased onto the new history, so the conflict is gone (that also marks the inline comments as outdated - replies are threaded on each).

Two maintainability items deferred to a follow-up to keep churn in shared lora.py minimal: the tile-merged-lora_A consolidation (P2 thread) and the host-side repeat efficiency note from the summary.

While validating tp2 we also hit a pre-existing bug from #14105: `FusedMoEWithLoRA` skips the `reduce_results` all-reduce that `FusedMoE.forward_impl` does after combine, so expert LoRA on any `reduce_results=True` MoE model returns per-rank partial sums under tp/ep (Mixtral/Qwen-MoE are unaffected - they reduce in model code). This PR is the first setup that can exercise that path, so the fix is included here as its own commit (a42ce2e1a); happy to split it out if you prefer.

Validation, fp16 vs HF+PEFT (teacher-forced logprobs + greedy): LFM2-8B-A1B and LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct both pass at tp1 with `--lora-target-modules all`; at `--tp 2` and `--tp 2 --ep 2` greedy output is token-identical to tp1.

Thanks @tugot17. Closing this because it has had no updates in 91 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

Reviewed the full diff (all 6 files) plus the surrounding LoRA stack (`mem_pool.py` buffer init, `lora.py` normalizers, `utils.py` target-module resolution, and the LoRA layer wrappers). The direction is solid and the HF+PEFT token-identical validation is convincing, but the review surfaced 4 issues that crash server startup or silently corrupt outputs (P0/P1 inline), plus 2 buffer-sizing problems and 2 maintainability concerns. Details are anchored inline; the first four are the ones I'd consider blocking.

Two additional notes not tied to a diff line:

- **Minor efficiency**: `tensor.repeat` in `_replicate_merged_in_proj_lora_a` materializes a 3x-tiled copy of every ShortConv `in_proj` `lora_A` that then lives in the adapter's CPU weight dict (and 3x-sized pinned-memory cache entries when overlap loading is on). Keeping `A` at rank `r` and copying it `c` times into rank-spaced buffer slices at load time (as the MoE path already does in `mem_pool.py`) would transfer the same bytes H2D without the persistent host-side blowup.
- **Rebase needed**: this branch currently shares no common ancestor with `main` (it predates the repo history migration), which is why GitHub reports the PR as conflicting — it will need a rebase onto the new history regardless of the review items above.

**[P0] Adding `"gate"` to `_KNOWN_LORA_TARGET_MODULES` breaks `--lora-target-modules all` for every other MoE model whose router is a `ReplicatedLinear` named `gate`** (qwen2_moe, qwen3_moe, mixtral, olmoe, ...).

`auto_detect_lora_target_modules` collects `LinearBase` leaf names and intersects with this set. Before this PR, `gate` was filtered out by the intersection; now it survives. `LoRAMemoryPool.init_buffer` then calls `get_hidden_dim("gate", ...)`, and since those models don't implement `get_hidden_dim`, the default fallback raises `NotImplementedError("get_hidden_dim not implemented for gate")` during memory-pool init — server fails to start on configurations that worked before this PR. (Models whose gate is a plain `nn.Module`, e.g. GLM4-MoE / DeepSeek `MoEGate`, are unaffected because auto-detect only picks up `LinearBase` leaves.)

Suggestion: only keep `gate` from auto-detect when the base model actually supports it (e.g. probe `base_model.get_hidden_dim("gate", 0)` / check for the method), or add a generic `gate` branch to the default `get_hidden_dim` fallback using `config.num_experts`.

**[P0] `--lora-target-modules all` crashes for LFM2 because `get_hidden_dim` has no `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` branches.**

Once a model defines `get_hidden_dim`, `lora/utils.py` dispatches *all* module-shape queries to it — bypassing the default fallback that does handle embeddings — and `--lora-target-modules all` unconditionally force-adds the embedding names. So `init_embedding_buffer → get_embedding_lora_A_shape → base_model.get_hidden_dim("embed_tokens", 0)` hits this `raise` at startup. The repro commands in the PR description only work because they enumerate target modules explicitly.

Same defect in `Lfm2MoeForCausalLM.get_hidden_dim` (`lfm2_moe.py`). Suggestion: add `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` branches, or delegate unknown names to the default util instead of raising.

Same issue as `lfm2.py`'s `get_hidden_dim` (see comment there): no `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` branches, so `--lora-target-modules all` crashes LFM2-MoE at memory-pool init before any of the router/expert/in_proj support added here is reachable.

**[P0] Router (`gate`) LoRA is broken under `tp > 1`: `"gate"` was not added to `REPLICATED_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES` in `lora/utils.py`.**

`mem_pool.get_lora_B_shape` finds `gate` in neither `ROW_PARALLELISM_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES` nor `REPLICATED_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES`, so it sizes the B buffer with the column-parallel assumption `divide(num_experts, tp_size)` — but the wrapping `ReplicatedLinearWithLoRA.slice_lora_b_weights` returns the full, unsliced `(num_experts, r)` tensor. For LFM2-8B-A1B (32 experts) with `--tp 2`, adapter load trips the buffer/weight shape assert (`(16, r)` vs `(32, r)`); with a `tp_size` that doesn't divide `num_experts`, `divide()` asserts already at pool init.

Fix: add `"gate"` to `REPLICATED_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES`.

**[P1] These `w1`/`w3`/`w2` mappings turn a loud failure into silent output corruption for models whose live modules are literally named `w1`/`w2`/`w3`** (e.g. InternLM2's `self.w2`).

For such a model, an adapter with `target_modules=["w2"]` now normalizes to `down_proj`: validation passes, buffers get allocated, and the renamed weights load without any skip warning — but module wrapping matches module basenames against the *normalized* target set, and basename `w2` is not in `{down_proj}`, so the module is never wrapped and the down-proj LoRA delta is silently dropped (wrong generations). Before this PR the same adapter failed loudly.

The rename is only correct for models whose runtime modules are actually named `gate_up_proj`/`down_proj` (LFM2 after this PR). Consider gating the normalization on the base model (mirroring how the weight-side `_rename_expert_w_to_proj` is scoped) rather than applying it globally.

**[P1] This allocates dense 3D `gate_up_proj`/`down_proj` LoRA buffers for *every* layer, but hybrid models only have a dense MLP on the first `num_dense_layers` layers.**

For LFM2-8B-A1B (24 layers, `num_dense_layers=2`, `intermediate_size=7168`) with expert LoRA targets, that's roughly ~0.6 GB of GPU memory (rank 64, 8 slots, bf16) held by buffers no wrapped module ever reads — directly shrinking KV-cache headroom. The shape fn already receives the layer idx, so allocation can be restricted to `idx < num_dense_layers` (zero-sized/skipped for MoE layers).

**[P1] This conflates attention `out_proj` (`head_dim * num_heads → hidden`) with ShortConv `out_proj` (`hidden → hidden`) and ignores `layer_idx`.**

The two coincide only while `head_dim * num_attention_heads == hidden_size`. The attention code in this file explicitly supports configs with an explicit `head_dim` where that equality breaks — and then conv-layer `out_proj` adapter weights `(r, hidden/tp)` won't match the `head_dim*num_heads/tp`-sized buffer, crashing on the shape assert at adapter load. `nemotron_h.get_hidden_dim` dispatches on the per-layer block type for exactly this reason; the same pattern applies here via the config's layer types. (Copied into `lfm2_moe.py` as well.)

**[P2, maintainability]** This is the fourth copy of the "tile a merged `lora_A` along the rank dim" pattern (`normalize_qkv_proj` x3, `_normalize_in_proj_qkvz` x4, `normalize_gate_up_proj` x2, now `in_proj` xc), each keyed on its own hardcoded module name — and only this copy guards on `tensor.shape[-2] == r`. A single shared `_tile_merged_lora_a(weights, name, c)` driven by `get_stacked_multiply` would keep the guards from diverging and spare the next packed projection a fifth copy.

**[P2, maintainability]** `get_hidden_dim`/`get_stacked_multiply` here are near-verbatim copies of the new methods in `lfm2.py` (`get_stacked_multiply` is byte-identical), and the two already differ subtly — dense `gate_up_proj` uses `_mlp_intermediate_size(config)` there vs raw `config.intermediate_size` here (correct for each model today, but exactly the kind of pair that rots). A small shared mixin/helper for the two LFM2 siblings would prevent fix-one-forget-the-other.
Fixed - auto-detect now drops `gate`; models opt in via `supported_lora_modules`.
Fixed - `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` branches added; `--lora-target-modules all` works end-to-end now (and is what the validation runs use).
Fixed together with the lfm2.py one - the shared branches now live in module-level helpers in lfm2.py that both models call.
Fixed as prescribed - `gate` added to `REPLICATED_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES`. tp2 greedy output is token-identical to tp1.
Fixed - the renames are now gated on the base model (`has_literal_w_modules`), on both the weight side and the target-module side, so literal-w models keep their previous loud-failure behavior.
Fixed - `get_hidden_dim` reports zero dims for `gate_up_proj`/`down_proj` on layers `>= num_dense_layers`, so sparse-layer buffers cost nothing.
Fixed - `out_proj` dims now dispatch on `config.layer_types[layer_idx]`, same pattern as nemotron_h.

Agreed, but deferring to a follow-up - the consolidation touches the qkv/gate_up/qkvz normalization paths every model shares and I want this PR's churn in core files minimal. The `in_proj` copy added here keeps the `rows != r` guard.

Fixed - common branches (attention/ShortConv/embeddings) moved to module-level helpers in lfm2.py that both models call explicitly; each model keeps its own MLP/MoE sizing branches, so the `_mlp_intermediate_size` vs raw `intermediate_size` difference is visible at the call sites.

@@ -1240,6 +1240,20 @@ def forward_impl(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor, topk_output: TopKOutput):
             dispatch_output=dispatch_output,
         )
 
+        return self.combine_and_reduce(combine_input, origin_hidden_states_dim)
+
+    def combine_and_reduce(
+        self, combine_input: CombineInput, origin_hidden_states_dim: int
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Combine dispatched expert outputs and apply the trailing
+        reduce_results all-reduce.
+
+        Shared by ``forward_impl`` and ``FusedMoEWithLoRA``, which replaces
+        the forward but must end the pipeline identically: under multi-rank
+        MoE (TP inner-shard or EP) each rank holds only a partial expert
+        output after combine, so skipping the reduction silently returns
+        partial sums.
+        """
         with use_symmetric_memory(
             get_tp_group(), disabled=not is_allocation_symmetric()
         ):

@@ -1043,6 +1043,7 @@ def _forward_with_lora(
         """
         # Get the base layer's dispatch and combine logic
         base_layer = self.base_layer
+        origin_hidden_states_dim = hidden_states.shape[-1]
 
         # Dispatch tokens (doesn't do much in the LoRA case)
         dispatch_output = base_layer.dispatcher.dispatch(
@@ -1067,9 +1068,11 @@ def _forward_with_lora(
                 dispatch_output, quant_info, lora_info=lora_info
             )
 
-        final_hidden_states = base_layer.dispatcher.combine(combine_input=combine_input)
-
-        return final_hidden_states
+        # End the pipeline exactly like FusedMoE.forward_impl (combine, trim
+        # to the original hidden dim, reduce_results all-reduce) — under
+        # multi-rank MoE, skipping the reduction silently returns per-rank
+        # partial expert sums.
+        return base_layer.combine_and_reduce(combine_input, origin_hidden_states_dim)
 
     def slice_lora_a_weights(self, A: torch.Tensor, tp_rank: int):
         return A

@@ -165,7 +165,7 @@ def _process_weight(self, name: str, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor):
         from sglang.srt.lora.utils import get_normalized_target_modules
 
         normalized_target_modules = get_normalized_target_modules(
-            self.config.target_modules
+            self.config.target_modules, self.base_model
         )
 
         # Remap PEFT "unembed_tokens" key to "lm_head" so the weight is
@@ -200,14 +200,24 @@ def _process_weight(self, name: str, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor):
             )
 
     def _normalize_weights(self):
+        from sglang.srt.lora.utils import has_literal_w_modules
+
+        # Skip the HF w1/w3/w2 renames for models that keep those literal
+        # module names at runtime (e.g. InternLM2) — see has_literal_w_modules.
+        rename_w_to_proj = self.base_model is None or not has_literal_w_modules(
+            self.base_model
+        )
         for layer in self.layers:
             weight_names = list(layer.weights.keys())
             self.normalize_qkv_proj(weight_names, layer.weights)
-            self._rename_expert_w_to_proj(layer.weights)
+            if rename_w_to_proj:

inline_comments.body:
**[P0] Adding `"gate"` to `_KNOWN_LORA_TARGET_MODULES` breaks `--lora-target-modules all` for every other MoE model whose router is a `ReplicatedLinear` named `gate`** (qwen2_moe, qwen3_moe, mixtral, olmoe, ...).

`auto_detect_lora_target_modules` collects `LinearBase` leaf names and intersects with this set. Before this PR, `gate` was filtered out by the intersection; now it survives. `LoRAMemoryPool.init_buffer` then calls `get_hidden_dim("gate", ...)`, and since those models don't implement `get_hidden_dim`, the default fallback raises `NotImplementedError("get_hidden_dim not implemented for gate")` during memory-pool init — server fails to start on configurations that worked before this PR. (Models whose gate is a plain `nn.Module`, e.g. GLM4-MoE / DeepSeek `MoEGate`, are unaffected because auto-detect only picks up `LinearBase` leaves.)

Suggestion: only keep `gate` from auto-detect when the base model actually supports it (e.g. probe `base_model.get_hidden_dim("gate", 0)` / check for the method), or add a generic `gate` branch to the default `get_hidden_dim` fallback using `config.num_experts`.

**[P0] `--lora-target-modules all` crashes for LFM2 because `get_hidden_dim` has no `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` branches.**

Once a model defines `get_hidden_dim`, `lora/utils.py` dispatches *all* module-shape queries to it — bypassing the default fallback that does handle embeddings — and `--lora-target-modules all` unconditionally force-adds the embedding names. So `init_embedding_buffer → get_embedding_lora_A_shape → base_model.get_hidden_dim("embed_tokens", 0)` hits this `raise` at startup. The repro commands in the PR description only work because they enumerate target modules explicitly.

Same defect in `Lfm2MoeForCausalLM.get_hidden_dim` (`lfm2_moe.py`). Suggestion: add `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` branches, or delegate unknown names to the default util instead of raising.

Same issue as `lfm2.py`'s `get_hidden_dim` (see comment there): no `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` branches, so `--lora-target-modules all` crashes LFM2-MoE at memory-pool init before any of the router/expert/in_proj support added here is reachable.

**[P0] Router (`gate`) LoRA is broken under `tp > 1`: `"gate"` was not added to `REPLICATED_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES` in `lora/utils.py`.**

`mem_pool.get_lora_B_shape` finds `gate` in neither `ROW_PARALLELISM_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES` nor `REPLICATED_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES`, so it sizes the B buffer with the column-parallel assumption `divide(num_experts, tp_size)` — but the wrapping `ReplicatedLinearWithLoRA.slice_lora_b_weights` returns the full, unsliced `(num_experts, r)` tensor. For LFM2-8B-A1B (32 experts) with `--tp 2`, adapter load trips the buffer/weight shape assert (`(16, r)` vs `(32, r)`); with a `tp_size` that doesn't divide `num_experts`, `divide()` asserts already at pool init.

Fix: add `"gate"` to `REPLICATED_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES`.

**[P1] These `w1`/`w3`/`w2` mappings turn a loud failure into silent output corruption for models whose live modules are literally named `w1`/`w2`/`w3`** (e.g. InternLM2's `self.w2`).

For such a model, an adapter with `target_modules=["w2"]` now normalizes to `down_proj`: validation passes, buffers get allocated, and the renamed weights load without any skip warning — but module wrapping matches module basenames against the *normalized* target set, and basename `w2` is not in `{down_proj}`, so the module is never wrapped and the down-proj LoRA delta is silently dropped (wrong generations). Before this PR the same adapter failed loudly.

The rename is only correct for models whose runtime modules are actually named `gate_up_proj`/`down_proj` (LFM2 after this PR). Consider gating the normalization on the base model (mirroring how the weight-side `_rename_expert_w_to_proj` is scoped) rather than applying it globally.

**[P1] This allocates dense 3D `gate_up_proj`/`down_proj` LoRA buffers for *every* layer, but hybrid models only have a dense MLP on the first `num_dense_layers` layers.**

For LFM2-8B-A1B (24 layers, `num_dense_layers=2`, `intermediate_size=7168`) with expert LoRA targets, that's roughly ~0.6 GB of GPU memory (rank 64, 8 slots, bf16) held by buffers no wrapped module ever reads — directly shrinking KV-cache headroom. The shape fn already receives the layer idx, so allocation can be restricted to `idx < num_dense_layers` (zero-sized/skipped for MoE layers).

**[P1] This conflates attention `out_proj` (`head_dim * num_heads → hidden`) with ShortConv `out_proj` (`hidden → hidden`) and ignores `layer_idx`.**

The two coincide only while `head_dim * num_attention_heads == hidden_size`. The attention code in this file explicitly supports configs with an explicit `head_dim` where that equality breaks — and then conv-layer `out_proj` adapter weights `(r, hidden/tp)` won't match the `head_dim*num_heads/tp`-sized buffer, crashing on the shape assert at adapter load. `nemotron_h.get_hidden_dim` dispatches on the per-layer block type for exactly this reason; the same pattern applies here via the config's layer types. (Copied into `lfm2_moe.py` as well.)

**[P2, maintainability]** This is the fourth copy of the "tile a merged `lora_A` along the rank dim" pattern (`normalize_qkv_proj` x3, `_normalize_in_proj_qkvz` x4, `normalize_gate_up_proj` x2, now `in_proj` xc), each keyed on its own hardcoded module name — and only this copy guards on `tensor.shape[-2] == r`. A single shared `_tile_merged_lora_a(weights, name, c)` driven by `get_stacked_multiply` would keep the guards from diverging and spare the next packed projection a fifth copy.

**[P2, maintainability]** `get_hidden_dim`/`get_stacked_multiply` here are near-verbatim copies of the new methods in `lfm2.py` (`get_stacked_multiply` is byte-identical), and the two already differ subtly — dense `gate_up_proj` uses `_mlp_intermediate_size(config)` there vs raw `config.intermediate_size` here (correct for each model today, but exactly the kind of pair that rots). A small shared mixin/helper for the two LFM2 siblings would prevent fix-one-forget-the-other.
Fixed - auto-detect now drops `gate`; models opt in via `supported_lora_modules`.
Fixed - `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` branches added; `--lora-target-modules all` works end-to-end now (and is what the validation runs use).
Fixed together with the lfm2.py one - the shared branches now live in module-level helpers in lfm2.py that both models call.
Fixed as prescribed - `gate` added to `REPLICATED_LINEAR_LORA_NAMES`. tp2 greedy output is token-identical to tp1.
Fixed - the renames are now gated on the base model (`has_literal_w_modules`), on both the weight side and the target-module side, so literal-w models keep their previous loud-failure behavior.
Fixed - `get_hidden_dim` reports zero dims for `gate_up_proj`/`down_proj` on layers `>= num_dense_layers`, so sparse-layer buffers cost nothing.
Fixed - `out_proj` dims now dispatch on `config.layer_types[layer_idx]`, same pattern as nemotron_h.

Agreed, but deferring to a follow-up - the consolidation touches the qkv/gate_up/qkvz normalization paths every model shares and I want this PR's churn in core files minimal. The `in_proj` copy added here keeps the `rows != r` guard.

reviews.body:
Reviewed the full diff (all 6 files) plus the surrounding LoRA stack (`mem_pool.py` buffer init, `lora.py` normalizers, `utils.py` target-module resolution, and the LoRA layer wrappers). The direction is solid and the HF+PEFT token-identical validation is convincing, but the review surfaced 4 issues that crash server startup or silently corrupt outputs (P0/P1 inline), plus 2 buffer-sizing problems and 2 maintainability concerns. Details are anchored inline; the first four are the ones I'd consider blocking.

Two additional notes not tied to a diff line:

- **Minor efficiency**: `tensor.repeat` in `_replicate_merged_in_proj_lora_a` materializes a 3x-tiled copy of every ShortConv `in_proj` `lora_A` that then lives in the adapter's CPU weight dict (and 3x-sized pinned-memory cache entries when overlap loading is on). Keeping `A` at rank `r` and copying it `c` times into rank-spaced buffer slices at load time (as the MoE path already does in `mem_pool.py`) would transfer the same bytes H2D without the persistent host-side blowup.
- **Rebase needed**: this branch currently shares no common ancestor with `main` (it predates the repo history migration), which is why GitHub reports the PR as conflicting — it will need a rebase onto the new history regardless of the review items above.
